subject: Peregrine Systems - westus3 latency + 5xx surge; propose geo-steer to eastus2
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@peregrine-sys.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@peregrine-sys.com
Date: 2028-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors - westus3 experiencing 5xx and huge latency

Hannah —

We just started seeing a spike in 500s and p95 latency moved from ~120ms to >2s across several routes in westus3 at ~09:05. Our product team is getting alerts and sessions are timing out. Attaching a quick snippet of error traces.

Things we've tried client-side: reduce concurrency, retry backoff — no change. Can your side confirm if there are any known capacity events in westus3? This is impacting Checkout flows for a handful of customers.

Attaching: peregrine_error_snippets.log (excerpt)

—Oliver
Senior SRE, Peregrine Systems
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@peregrine-sys.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-29T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors - westus3 experiencing 5xx and huge latency

Oliver — thanks for the quick report and the log snippet. I'm pulling the platform telemetry now. Can you confirm the customer-facing tenant ID and a sample request ID when you see the 500s? That will speed root-cause.

Immediate plan options:
- Short-term: geo-steer a percentage of Peregrine traffic from westus3 -> eastus2 (we can do 50% then ramp).
- Mid-term: failover to a compatible model variant/instance pool in eastus2 while we investigate westus3 node health.

I've looped in on-call (Dylan) to validate capacity and run the geo-steer if you approve. Also adding CS for customer comms (Marissa).

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Oliver Grant <oliver@peregrine-sys.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-29T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors - westus3 experiencing 5xx and huge latency

Hi — I’m on call. Quick diagnostics: we see an increase in request queue length and elevated GPU kernel time on westus3 cluster nodes serving the cu45-8bit model pool (hostpool id: hp-westus3-cu45). p95 token time jumped to ~2.3s at 09:04.

Proposal (immediate):
1) Execute geo-steer: route 60% of Peregrine’s traffic to eastus2 where we have warm capacity (compatible model variant cu45-8q).
2) Enable temporary cache affinity (prefix KV eviction) to reduce cross-region cold loads.
3) Monitor SLOs for 20 minutes; if errors drop, ramp to 90% and then fully cut over.

I will not change routing without customer OK and exec visibility. Requesting explicit approval to enact geo-steer now.

Attachments: dashboard_westus3_0900-1000.png (ops dashboard snapshot)

—Dylan
On-call: Infra Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-29T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Peregrine Systems - westus3 latency + 5xx surge; propose geo-steer to eastus2 — exec visibility requested

Folks — forwarding a P0 from Peregrine (tenant: pereg-9742). Westus3 cluster has elevated GPU times and queueing causing widespread 500s and p95 spikes. On-call proposes immediate geo-steer to eastus2 (60% -> ramp). Customer is ready to approve but I need leadership visibility for both operational and credit/contract considerations.

Questions for leadership:
- Approve geo-steer now? It will increase egress and per-token costs during the ramp (estimate: +$1.2k/hr while ramping).
- If we fully cut traffic and perform a failover, do we pre-approve a one-time credit for the customer for downtime? (Marissa, want to coordinate comms once we know timeline.)

Timeline: On-call requests approval to start geo-steer in the next 5 minutes pending customer thumbs up.

—Hannah
From: Oliver Grant <oliver@peregrine-sys.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@peregrine-sys.com
Date: 2028-08-29T09:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Peregrine Systems - westus3 latency + 5xx surge; propose geo-steer to eastus2

Hannah/Dylan — please proceed with the geo-steer immediately. We approve an initial 60% bump and will monitor. Request you keep the support channel updated with minute-by-minute changes; our product team is standing by.

Oliver
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver@peregrine-sys.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-29T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Peregrine Systems - westus3 latency + 5xx surge; propose geo-steer to eastus2 — mitigation complete (interim)

Update: We executed the geo-steer at 09:34 and ramped to 60% over 2 minutes. Observed error rate drop from ~11% to 0.8% within the first 6 minutes; p95 latency returned to ~140ms for steered traffic. We ramped to 90% at 09:52 after confirming stability and left 10% on westus3 for final draining.

Next steps / action items:
- Infra: investigate underlying kernel regression on hp-westus3-cu45 (assigned to infra team; Jira: INFRA-8721).
- Product: validate model-variant parity between westus3 and eastus2 (Vanessa).
- CS: coordinate customer comms and any goodwill credit (Marissa).
- Postmortem target: 48 hours (owner: Dylan).

Attachments: post-geo-steer-stats.csv (summary attached to internal Jira ticket).

—Dylan
